idea-plugin.name: Oracle JDK License Gate
idea-plugin.description:
Moving to Temurin, Corretto, Zulu or another OpenJDK build? See which Java every part of your project pulls — GitHub Actions setup-java, Dockerfile base images, Gradle and Maven toolchains, SDKMAN (.sdkmanrc), asdf / mise (.tool-versions), dev containers, Homebrew, winget and Chocolatey — with the Oracle-licensed ones flagged on today's date and the free Eclipse Temurin (Adoptium) or Amazon Corretto line for each place.

Why the date matters: Oracle's No-Fee Terms (NFTC) cover a Java LTS release until one year after the next LTS ships. The free window for JDK 21 closed on 2026-09-16 and for JDK 17 on 2024-09-19; Oracle JDK 8 and 11 builds are under the Oracle Technology Network license (development and test only). After that, Oracle prices Java SE on total headcount, contractors included.

  • Java map (free, local): Tools → Oracle JDK License Gate: Java Map. Every place this project chooses a Java build, the JDKs this IDE runs it on (read from each JDK's own release file), and the Temurin / Corretto line for each place.
  • Inline check (free): 18 rules on Dockerfiles, CI workflows, Gradle and Maven files, SDKMAN, asdf and shell scripts, as you open them. Each finding names the license and the free line that replaces it. Runs inside the IDE: no Node.js, nothing leaves your machine.
  • Dated project report (paid): every Oracle-licensed line, the free line for each, the JDKs the IDE knows and the SHA-256 of every file read, written as a file for your team lead, an auditor or CI. Licence key $29 once; team key $149 once (5 seats, every ReadyStack linter). Get a key at getreadystack.com/tools/oracle-jdk-license-gate.

Same 18 rules as the ReadyStack VS Code extension. Privacy: licence keys are checked against getreadystack.com; if usage statistics sharing is on in the IDE, one anonymous count per action (tool name and action only, never file content). Set READYSTACK_NO_TELEMETRY=1 to turn it off.
